undock.release_note: The magnet pairs are slid sideways by a cam ring before the pumps pull back: 6 x 18.2 N of shear instead of the 105 N pull.

checks.text: Gel surface inside the shell 32 mm under the outer waterline: the dome air sits at 313 Pa and holds the gel down (diving bell).
The opening is under water: its top is 52 mm below the waterline and 20 mm below the inner gel surface.
Gel at the open opening: density excess gives 6.5 Pa of drive against a 25 Pa yield stress, so the gel stays in the shell.
Kit held in place after release: kit density 945 kg/m3, so the gel needs 2.5 Pa to hold the kit against rising (gel has 25 Pa), and the saddle feet sit in three cups.
Every G-code point is inside the DexArm reach (200 mm stem, base on a 140 mm shelf rail): worst position error 0.00 mm, 0 points at a joint limit.

After the kit is placed the stem (12G needle, then the 6 mm tube) misses the kit parts except at 1 point by a pump end, 0.9 mm into the outline, where the first beads lap onto the saddle lip by design.
DexArm push stays under its 0.5 kg payload (4.9 N): peak 2.49 N.
ECO62 push stays under its 2 kg payload (19.6 N): peak 2.49 N.

Click: the magnets pull the tail in the last 20 mm; it meets the 3 mm silicone bumpers at 321 mm/s, contact peak 603 N over six bumpers; six pairs then hold 105 N against 10 N of dome air on the face.
The newborn floats: 73 % of the 1.04 L body is under water, 25 mm above the surface.
Stem bending at the peak push (2.5 N): 12G needle, 40 mm out of the tube, 76 MPa; 6 x 4 mm push tube, 140 mm lever, 20 MPa; about 200 MPa yield for 304 stainless.
